clue.text: Journey's end is across river

indicators.note: the word for an end stretches across, spanning the river's letter

parts.note: an end or tip, as of a finger

explanation.surface: A traveller's destination lies on the far side of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Read "Journey's" as "Journey is": the definition comes first and "is" links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a short excursion, a synonym for a journey.

clue.text: Reliable type embraces one hard hit

indicators.note: the reliable person's word holds the numeral within its arms

parts.note: a trump, in dated slang, is a dependable, good-hearted person
I is the Roman numeral for one
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A dependable sort hugs someone who has just been struck hard.
explanation.walkthrough: "hit" looks like a verb in the surface but it is the noun: a great success.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a resounding success, just as a show or record can be a smash hit.

clue.text: Endless sexual misbehaviour closes clinic

indicators.note: the misbehaviour word shuts in, enclosing, the clinic's letters

parts.note: incest is forbidden sexual relations within a family
SAN is short for sanatorium, a medical clinic

explanation.surface: Unending sexual scandal forces a clinic to shut its doors.
explanation.walkthrough: "Endless" seems to describe the misbehaviour, but it is the definition; "closes" is not shuts down but encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incessant never stops, so it is without end.

clue.text: Standard response of class to character

parts.note: a form is a school class, as in the sixth form
a letter is a written character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A school report comments on how a class responds to a pupil's character.
explanation.definitionFit: A form letter is a stock reply sent unchanged to many correspondents, so it is a standard response.

clue.text: Arranges frontiers to exclude British

indicators.note: the frontiers word is to leave out the abbreviation for British

parts.note: borders are frontiers between countries

explanation.surface: A government sets up border controls designed to keep Britons out.
explanation.definitionFit: To order things is to put them in sequence, that is to arrange them.

clue.text: Small fight after game

indicators.note: the fight word follows, coming after, the game word

parts.note: a match is a sporting game
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A minor scuffle breaks out once the game is over.
explanation.definitionFit: As a modifier, matchbox describes something tiny, like a matchbox car or a matchbox-sized flat.

clue.text: Roosevelt opposes royal memorials

parts.note: Eleanor Roosevelt was the US First Lady married to Franklin D. Roosevelt
to cross someone is to oppose or thwart them

explanation.surface: A Roosevelt objects to monuments honouring a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an American politician against royalty; the answer is the stone crosses Edward I raised in England for his queen, Eleanor of Castile.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward I erected twelve such crosses marking where his queen's funeral cortege rested, so they are monuments to royalty.

clue.text: Sets of bones one's rodent turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters for one's and rodent are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: one is I, and one's is read as one is, giving I plus S
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: Someone's pet rat has turned up a few skeletons.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsi is the plural of tarsus, the group of ankle bones, so each is a set of bones.

clue.text: Love to see party of Africans in capital

indicators.note: the party's letters go in the middle of the capital's name

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
the ANC is the African National Congress, the South African political party

explanation.surface: Couples travel to Rome to watch an African political party in session.
explanation.definitionFit: Romance is love affection between partners, a synonym for love.

clue.text: Nurse may tuck in this corporal, then is free

indicators.note: the words corporal then is are set free and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A nurse slips a corporal into bed, then he is released.
explanation.walkthrough: "free" seems to describe the corporal but signals the rearrangement; the definition plays on a nurse tucking in a patient, when it is the sheet she tucks.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital corner is the neat diagonal fold made when tucking a bed sheet under the mattress, a nursing technique.

clue.text: As clique, they're not alone

definitions.meaning: an exclusive inner set of fashionable people
people surrounded by a throng are among others, part of the mass

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a fashionable exclusive circle, and read literally describes people who are among a crowd and so not alone.

clue.text: Soldiers that you captured missed at the front, it was proved

indicators.note: the old word for you takes the soldiers prisoner, holding them inside

parts.note: thee is the archaic object form of you
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word missed is taken

explanation.surface: Soldiers taken prisoner by you were missed from the front line, it was shown.
explanation.walkthrough: "missed at the front" looks like part of the battle story but just supplies the first letter of missed.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a theorem is a statement that has been demonstrated by logical argument.

clue.text: Girl's brief worry, getting the wrong idea

indicators.note: a brief word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Miss is a title for an unmarried girl or young woman; the 's is no letter
apprehension is anxiety or worry

explanation.surface: A young woman's short-lived anxiety comes from misunderstanding something.
explanation.walkthrough: "brief" looks like it qualifies the worry but cuts the last letter from the girl's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A misapprehension is a mistaken belief, a misunderstanding.

clue.text: Fine condition of lake in open country

indicators.note: the lake's letter sits within the word for open country

parts.note: a heath is open uncultivated land
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A lake in open countryside is in excellent shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Health is the state of being well, so good health is a fine condition.

clue.text: Teaching about downfall of girl in old duchy

indicators.note: the teaching word goes around, about, the downfall word

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge passed on by teaching
rain is a fall of water from the sky, a downpour

explanation.surface: Instruction concerning the ruin of a young woman in a historic duchy.
explanation.walkthrough: "downfall" suggests ruin but just means rainfall. The definition does double duty: a girl's name and the duchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorraine is a female given name and also the former duchy in north-eastern France.

clue.text: Entrant is thrown out at once

indicators.note: the letters of Entrant is are thrown about and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A newcomer is ejected immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Instanter is a legal Latin adverb meaning immediately.

clue.text: Put up with fault in acts for the moment

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate or put up with it
a sin is a moral fault or wrong

explanation.surface: Tolerating a flaw in someone's actions for now.
explanation.walkthrough: "in" here is just a link, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stands in deputises temporarily, filling a role for the time being.

clue.text: One passed on visiting stomach-turning butcher

indicators.note: the tummy word turns round and reads backwards

parts.note: tum is informal for stomach
I is the Roman numeral for one
the following pieces call on, coming after, the stomach word

explanation.surface: A dead man calling on a stomach-churning scene of slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: "stomach-turning" reads as revolting but splits: the stomach word reversed, giving MUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher something is to hack it about, to maim or disfigure it.

clue.text: Where soldiers may eat in a port

parts.note: a mess is a military dining hall
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dockside spot where troops could grab a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Messina is a harbour city in Sicily, on the strait facing mainland Italy.

clue.text: Annoyance: duck stopping runs being scored quickly

indicators.note: the runs letter is plugged into the annoyance and duck, which stop it up

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance or annoyance
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A batsman's irritation as a duck stops him adding runs to the scoreboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of a duck and runs scored covers a musical sense: "being scored" hints at a written score.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical direction to play very fast.

clue.text: Strange, how policeman relaxes

definitions.meaning: unconventional or out of the ordinary
an officer resting is away from his patrol route

explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat means unconventional or eccentric, and a constable at ease is off his patrol beat.

clue.text: Spring from prison gang heartlessly incarcerated

indicators.note: the gang's letters are locked up inside the prison word

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail

indicators.note: the gang word loses its middle letter, its heart

parts.note: a mob is a gang of people

explanation.surface: A heartless gang is locked away, and someone escapes from prison.
explanation.walkthrough: "Spring" looks like an escape from prison; it is the definition, a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambol is a playful skip or leap, a synonym for a spring.

clue.text: As cowardly soldier, join flash regiment, initially shuffled to planning group

indicators.note: join, flash and the regiment's first letter are shuffled into a new order
only the opening letter of regiment is used

parts.note: a staff is the group of officers who plan military operations

explanation.surface: A coward enlists in a showy regiment and is reassigned to headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuffled' rearranges JOINFLASHR into SIRJOHNFAL. Falstaff is Shakespeare's boastful, cowardly knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's fat knight fakes death at Shrewsbury and preaches that discretion is the better part of valour.

clue.text: Having hoisted ladder, heads for usual platform

parts.note: a ladder is a run in stockings or tights

indicators.note: only the leading letters of usual and platform are taken

explanation.surface: Someone climbs a ladder and makes for their regular stage.
explanation.walkthrough: "ladder" suggests climbing, but in British usage it is a run in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag that has been run up the mast has been raised, hauled aloft.

clue.text: What's collected from bookie, not the first chance to score

indicators.note: the bookie word drops its first letter

parts.note: winnings are the money a bettor collects from a bookmaker

explanation.surface: A punter collects winnings from the bookmaker, but not on the first race.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an innings is a team's or batsman's turn at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket innings is a team's turn to bat and so its opportunity to make runs.

clue.text: Take into mouth newly-made herb tea

indicators.note: herb and tea are made afresh, their letters put in a new order

explanation.surface: Sipping a freshly brewed herbal tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe is to draw air in, which one can do through the mouth.

clue.text: Happen not to be captivated by what's fruity, it seems

indicators.note: the negative verb is held captive inside the fruity word

parts.note: apply is taken as appley, tasting like an apple
if they happen not to be there, they are not, contracted to are not

explanation.surface: Someone seems not to be charmed by anything fruity.
explanation.walkthrough: "captivated by" reads as charmed but is the container signal; "fruity" is stretched to mean apple-like, which bloggers called cheeky but fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparently means seemingly, judging by how things appear.

clue.text: Dirty mess in poet's cave

definitions.meaning: British slang for filth or squalor
a literary word for a grotto, used in verse

explanation.definitionFit: Grot is British slang for grime, and in poetry it is a shortened form of grotto, a cave.
